messages:
Sam: quick check-in — ran a pass of speculative decoding on nova-13b-quant (4-bit qnt) with the new fast-prefetch path. rough numbers: ~1.9x token throughput vs baseline, median p50 latency down ~35ms on short prompts.
Mai: nice. what workload / prompt mix did you use? random chat sims or codebench?
Sam: mostly mixed: 60% short chat (<=64 toks), 30% assistant multi-turn (200-400 toks), 10% codegen snippets from internal codebench. saw most wins on the short chat bucket.
Ravi: any quality regressions? did you run our eval-suite (constancy + instruction-following) or human evals?
Sam: ran the automated eval-suite first. small regressions on instruction-following metrics for temperature=0.8 sampling — approx 1.8% drop on our ROUGE-style pass@k for the assistant set. deterministic/top-k greedy had negligible delta.
Ben: that suggests sampling+speculative interplay. was speculative rollout using a different sampling seed/ordering?
Sam: config snippet:
```
speculative: true
speculative_k: 2
speculative_threshold: 0.85
sampling: {
  method: "top-p",
  p: 0.92,
  temp: 0.8
}
quant: 4bit-gptq
batching: dynamic
```
Mai: can you try lowering speculative_threshold to 0.7 or reducing k to 1 and re-run the instruction suite? If quality improves with small perf hit that's probably safer for canary.
Sam: yes will run an ablation tomorrow. also want to try disabling prefix caching during speculative canary — curious if cache staleness is contributing to divergence.
Ravi: for evaluation methodology — let's add token-level agreement and LM logit overlap (cosine of top-16 logits) to the suite. that will help show if speculation changes distribution even when discrete metrics are similar.
Ben: +1. Also flag chronometric metrics: percentage of outputs that trigger fallback to slow path. ops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled at 2026-03-22T09:00Z if tests pass.
Sam: planned experiments: 1) reduce k to 1 2) threshold 0.7 and 0.8 3) disable prefix cache 4) run with seed sweep (5 seeds) for sampling stability. will post numbers here.
Mai: for human evals, pick 200 instruction prompts where automated score dropped and re-rate for helpfulness/accuracy. we need to confirm significance.
Ravi: if human eval shows subjective drop, iterate on fallback policy (use greedy fallback when sampling entropy > X).
Sam: noted. quick note on infra: memory tail not an issue on these runs; quantized model fits comfortably. will also run on Dedicated nodes to compare scheduling jitter.
Ben: awesome. thanks Sam. please include raw eval artifacts (csv + logits) in the shared bucket and ping me when uploading.
Sam: will do, tagging results here when ready. :thumbsup:
